en: Test for English Majors 2017.
zh: 2017年英语专业全国统一考试。

en: Grade 8.
zh: 专业八级。

en: Part 1. Listening Comprehension.
zh: 第一部分：听力理解。

en: Section A. mini-lecture.
zh: A节：短讲。

en: In this section, you will hear a mini-lecture.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段短讲。

en: You will hear the mini-lecture once only.
zh: 这段短讲只播放一遍。

en: While listening to the mini-lecture, please complete the gap-filling task on answer sheet 1 and write no more than three words for each gap.
zh: 请边听短讲，边完成答题卡一上的填空任务；每空填写不超过三个词。

en: Make sure the words you fill in are both grammatically and semantically acceptable.
zh: 请确保填入的词在语法和语义上都恰当。

en: You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
zh: 你可以用空白纸做笔记。

en: You have 30 seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览填空任务。

en: Now listen to the mini-lecture.
zh: 现在请听短讲。

en: When it is over, you will be given three minutes to check your work.
zh: 短讲结束后，你将有三分钟检查作答。

en: The modes of language.
zh: 语言的表达方式。

en: Good morning, everyone.
zh: 大家早上好。

en: In our last lecture, I was talking about language as part of a semiotic system.
zh: 上一讲中，我谈到语言是我们符号系统的一部分。

en: And today, I’m going to move on to another topic, that is, the modes of language.
zh: 今天我要转向另一个话题，也就是语言的表达方式。

en: As you may know, messages are transmitted in human language most frequently through two primary modes: speech and writing.
zh: 大家可能知道，人类语言传递信息最常用的两种基本方式是口语和书面语。

en: Well, you know there is also a third mode which is not that frequently used as speech and writing.
zh: 当然，还有第三种方式，只是没有口语和书面语那么常用。

en: The third mode is called signing, which is used by deaf people.
zh: 第三种方式叫手语，是失聪人士使用的。

en: But in today’s lecture, we will just focus on speech and writing and the specific features of these two modes.
zh: 不过，今天我们只讨论口语和书面语，以及这两种表达方式各自的特点。

en: In linguistics, it is commonly noted that speech is primary and writing secondary.
zh: 在语言学中，人们通常认为口语是首要的，书面语是次要的。

en: Linguists take this position because all languages are spoken except those dead languages such as Latin, which is only existent in written form.
zh: 语言学家持这种观点，是因为除了拉丁语这类如今只以书面形式存在的死语言之外，所有语言都有口语形式。

en: All children will naturally acquire the spoken version of a language if they are exposed to it.
zh: 只要接触到一种语言，所有儿童都会自然习得它的口语形式。

en: They acquire the spoken form of their mother tongue during the formative period of language acquisition.
zh: 他们在语言习得的关键成长阶段，掌握母语的口语形式。

en: However, to become literate, a child will need some kind of formal schooling in reading and writing.
zh: 然而，要具备读写能力，儿童就需要接受某种正规的读写教育。

en: In many respects, we might call speech “primary” and writing “secondary”.
zh: 在许多方面，我们或许可以称口语为“首要的”，称书面语为“次要的”。

en: It implies that writing has a second-class status when compared with speech.
zh: 但这会暗示，相较于口语，书面语的地位低人一等。

en: In fact, it is more accurate to view the two modes as having different but complementary roles.
zh: 事实上，更准确的看法是：这两种方式发挥着不同但互补的作用。

en: For instance, in most legal systems, while an oral contract is legally binding, a written contract is preferred.
zh: 例如，在大多数法律制度中，虽然口头合同具有法律约束力，人们仍更倾向于书面合同。

en: The reason is simple.
zh: 原因很简单。

en: Unlike speech, writing provides a permanent record of the contract.
zh: 与口语不同，书面语可以为合同留下永久记录。

en: Thus, if the terms of the contract are disputed, the written record of the contract can be consulted and interpreted.
zh: 因此，如果人们对合同条款发生争议，就可以查阅并解释合同的书面记录。

en: Disputes over an oral contract will involve one person’s recollection of the contract versus another person’s.
zh: 而围绕口头合同的争议，会变成双方各执一词，比较各自对合同内容的记忆。

en: While writing may be the preferred mode for a contract, in many other contexts, speech will be more appropriate.
zh: 虽然书面语可能更适合订立合同，但在其他许多情境中，口语会更加合适。

en: Because the most common type of speech – face-to-face conversations
zh: 最常见的口语形式——面对面交谈

en: – is highly interactive, this mode is well suited to many social contexts,
zh: ——具有很强的互动性，因此很适用于许多社交情境，

en: such as casual conversations over lunch, business transactions in a grocery store, discussions between students and teachers in a classroom.
zh: 例如午餐时闲聊、杂货店里的买卖交流，以及课堂上师生之间的讨论。

en: And in these contexts, interactive dialogues have many advantages over writing.
zh: 在这些情境中，互动式对话比书面语具有许多优势。

en: For instance, individuals engaged in conversation can ask for immediate clarification if there is a question about something said;
zh: 例如，交谈者如果对刚听到的内容有疑问，可以立即要求澄清；

en: in a letter to a friend, in contrast, such immediacy is lacking.
zh: 相比之下，给朋友写信就缺少这种即时性。

en: When speaking to one another, speakers are face-to-face and can therefore see how individuals react to what is said;
zh: 交谈时，说话双方彼此面对面，因此能看到对方对话语的反应；

en: on the other hand, writing creates a distance between writer and reader, preventing the writer from getting any immediate reaction from the reader.
zh: 而写作使作者与读者之间存在距离，作者无法得到读者的即时反馈。

en: Speech is oral, thus making it possible to use intonation to emphasize words or phrases and express emotion.
zh: 口语通过声音表达，因此可以运用语调来强调词语或短语，并传达情感。

en: Of course, one might say that writing has punctuation.
zh: 当然，有人可能会说，书面语有标点符号。

en: Well, it can express only a small proportion of the features that intonation has.
zh: 但标点符号只能表达语调所能体现的一小部分特征。

en: Because speech is created “on-line,” it is produced quickly and easily.
zh: 因为口语是在表达过程中即时生成的，所以产生得既快又容易。

en: This may result in many “ungrammatical” constructions, but rarely do these rough sentences cause miscommunications.
zh: 这可能产生许多“不符合语法”的结构，但这些不够严整的句子很少造成沟通障碍。

en: You know, if there is a misunderstanding, it can be easily corrected.
zh: 即使发生误解，也很容易纠正。

en: On the contrary, writing is much more deliberate.
zh: 相反，书面表达需要经过更多深思熟虑。

en: It requires planning, editing and thus taking much more time to produce on the part of the writer.
zh: 它要求写作者进行构思和修改，因此需要花费更多时间才能完成。

en: Because of all these characteristics of writing,
zh: 由于书面语的这些特点，

en: if an individual desires a casual, intimate encounter with a friend, he or she is more likely to meet personally than write a letter.
zh: 如果一个人想与朋友轻松、亲近地交流，通常更愿意亲自见面，而不是写信。

en: In this case, writing a letter to a friend might turn out to be too formal.
zh: 在这种情况下，给朋友写信反而可能显得过于正式。

en: Of course, in today’s world, the highly developed technology has made such encounters possible with “instant messaging” over a computer or smartphone.
zh: 当然，在当今世界，高度发展的技术让人们可以通过电脑或智能手机上的“即时通信”来进行这类交流。

en: And if someone wishes to have such an encounter with a friend living many miles away, then this kind of on-line written “chat” can mimic a face-to-face conversation.
zh: 如果想与相隔很远的朋友交流，这种网上文字“聊天”就可以模拟面对面的交谈。

en: But because such conversations are a hybrid of speech and writing, they still lack the intimacy and immediacy of a face-to-face conversation.
zh: 但由于这种交谈是口语和书面语的混合形式，它仍然缺少面对面交流的亲近感和即时性。

en: While speech and writing are often viewed as discrete modes, it is important for us to note that there is a continuum between speech and writing.
zh: 虽然口语和书面语往往被视为彼此独立的表达方式，但我们必须注意，两者之间存在一个连续体。

en: While speech is in general more interactive than writing, various kinds of spoken and written English display various degrees of interactivity.
zh: 总体来说，口语比书面语更具互动性，不过，不同类型的英语口语和书面语所呈现的互动程度也各不相同。

en: For instance, various linguistic markers of interactive discourse, such as first- and second-person pronouns, contractions,
zh: 例如，互动话语的多种语言标记，包括第一、第二人称代词、缩略形式，

en: and private verbs such as think and feel,
zh: 以及think和feel这类表示内心活动的动词，

en: occurred very frequently in telephone and face-to-face conversations but less frequently in spontaneous speeches, interviews, and broadcasts.
zh: 在电话和面对面交谈中出现得非常频繁，在即兴演讲、访谈和广播中则少一些。

en: In addition, some kinds of writing, such as academic prose and official documents, exhibited few markers of interactive discourse.
zh: 此外，学术文章和官方文件等某些书面文本中，互动话语的标记很少。

en: But other kinds of written texts, particularly personal letters, ranked higher on the scale of interactivity than many of the spoken texts.
zh: 但另一些书面文本，特别是私人信件，其互动程度高于许多口语文本。

en: In other words, how language is structured depends less on whether it is spoken or written but more on how it is being used.
zh: 换句话说，语言的组织方式与其说取决于口头还是书面形式，不如说取决于它如何被使用。

en: For example, a personal letter, even though it is written,
zh: 例如，私人信件虽然是书面的，

en: will contain linguistic features marking interactivity because the writer of a letter wishes to interact with the receiver of the letter.
zh: 却含有体现互动性的语言特征，因为写信者希望与收信者交流。

en: On the other hand, in an interview, the goal is not to interact necessarily but to get information from the person being interviewed.
zh: 另一方面，访谈的目的未必是互动，而是从受访者那里获取信息。

en: Therefore, though interviews are spoken, they have fewer markers of interactivity and contain more features typically associated with written texts.
zh: 因此，访谈虽然采用口语形式，互动标记却较少，反而含有更多通常与书面文本相关的特征。

en: OK, to sum up, we have been dealing with the modes of language in today’s lecture.
zh: 好，总结一下，今天这堂课我们讨论了语言的表达方式。

en: The two most frequently used modes are speech and writing.
zh: 最常用的两种方式是口语和书面语。

en: As two different modes of language, speech and writing have their own characteristics.
zh: 作为两种不同的语言表达方式，口语和书面语各有特点。

en: Speech is a preferred mode in many social contexts where interactivity is needed.
zh: 在许多需要互动的社交情境中，口语是更合适的方式。

en: Of course, when a formal, stable record is preferred, writing should be an appropriate mode.
zh: 当然，如果需要正式、稳定的记录，书面语应该是适宜的表达方式。

en: Finally, I have also emphasized that there is a continuum between speech and writing.
zh: 最后，我也强调了口语与书面语之间存在一个连续体。

en: In the following lecture, we will concentrate on the linguistic structures of language.
zh: 下一讲，我们将重点讨论语言的结构。

en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢大家。

en: Now you have three minutes to check your work.
zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。

en: This is the end of Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节短讲到此结束。
